commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1941826: Don't guard for number types in emitGuardIsNumber. r=jandem

This aligns Warp transpilation with CacheIR, because in CacheIR `NumberOperandId`
can mean either `Double` or `Int32`. (There isn't yet an explicit
`DoubleOperandId` to denote a value is guaranteed to be a Double.)

Float32 optimisations can be more easily applied when `MToDouble` isn't emitted
and we also no longer need the `MToDouble::canProduceFloat32` override added in
D215775.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D234348

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1942648: Support MSign with Int32 input and Double output. r=jandem

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D234936
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 8354ae880cf5 on top of intro 9385dab26b90 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (TypeConfusion): The change to emitGuardIsNumber removed automatic conversion of Int32/Float32 inputs to Double. This broke an implicit assumption in visitSign that when input and output types differ, the input is always Double and output is Int32. When MSign now receives Int32 input with Double output, the else branch incorrectly asserts the opposite and uses LSignDI (Double input, Int32 output) instead of a proper LSignID (Int32 input, Double output). This causes: 1) Writing to an unrelated general purpose register instead of the allocated float output register, 2) The allocated float register retains its previous value, enabling type confusion where uninitialized/stale float data can be read as legitimate values. Root cause: The change in emitGuardIsNumber (bug 1941826) removed automatic conversion of Int32/Float32 inputs to Double for number guards. This was intended to enable better Float32 optimizations. However, downstream code in visitSign had hardcoded assumptions that when MSign input and output types differ, the input is always Double and output is Int32. The change created a new valid case (Int32 input, Double output) that was not handled, causing assertion failures and type confusion when the wrong LIR instruction was selected.
